persona: Juniper "June" Alvarez, 10, fourth grade in north Seattle, second season of rec soccer (U10 Purple Pumas), plays defense because "you don't have to be fast, you just have to be annoying." No phone of her own. Plays on Mom's phone at breakfast or the family iPad after homework.
first_week:
Monday: Dad shows me at breakfast because he saw it in the team parent chat. The arcade machine look is SO cool, it looks like the Pac-Man at the pizza place. Six pentagons. One says "Rangers FC" and I don't know what that is. One says "throw-in" and I know that one! I tap it, I'm right, and the pentagon goes black. I yell. Next I tap "Messi" because I know him. Right again. Then everything left is words I can't read fast, like "Bundesliga." Dad says just guess, I guess, it goes red and shakes and I'm out. Nil. I'm kind of mad, but the answer filled in and the little line under it taught me something, so OK.
Tuesday: I ask for Mom's phone myself. Second card is about some French club. Out. Nil again. I don't want to text Nil to anybody.
Wednesday: I get a kid slang one about the orange slices being bussin and I laugh so hard. I also get an offside one and I know it because Coach Dee yelled about it Saturday. I fill the whole first ball and it says GOAL. I make Mom text it to Dad at work and to my Abuela. Dad texts back "BRACE OR BUST" and now it's a thing.
Thursday: Nil on a hard one in the first ball. I almost don't care anymore.
Friday: Dad and I play together. I pick the tiles, he helps me read. We get a Goal. Most fun day because we argued about the answer.
Weekend: I forget Saturday because of my game. Sunday I remember and get a Goal. If I'd gotten Nil Thursday AND Friday I think I'd have stopped by now.
play_daily: Maybe. On my own, leaning no. With Dad at breakfast, yes. I come back if I get a Goal most days. If I get Nil three days in a row because the first ball has hard cards about leagues I've never heard of, I'm done and I go back to my drawing app. What brings me back is the breakfast thing with Dad and beating his score, not the trivia by itself.
share: I don't have a phone, so Mom texts it for me. Goal or better goes to Dad at work, my Abuela in Tucson, and my best friend Priya from the Pumas through her mom. I would NEVER send a Nil. The red square where I went out feels like being shown up, so I'd want it to look like the black balls I got, not a big red mistake. I'd send it more if the text showed the black pentagons I filled even when I didn't finish a ball, like "I got 4 of 6," so a bad day still looks like something. I'd send it less if it had a bunch of numbers or a long link.
love: The arcade machine. It looks like a real game, not homework.
Turning a pentagon black. It feels like coloring in the soccer ball.
Picking my own tile. I pick the words I know first, and that's my strategy.
Kid slang cards. Grown-ups get them wrong and I get them right.
Rules cards like offside and throw-ins, because I can use them at my game Saturday.
The answer filling in after I miss, plus the little line that tells me why. I actually remember those.
No timer. I read slow and nobody rushes me.
Same cards as Dad, so we can talk about card number whatever at dinner.
turn_offs: Going out on card 1 or 2 almost every day. That's not a game, that's just losing.
Hook words I can't read or say, like Bundesliga, Borussia, Ligue 1. I skip them, and then they're the only tiles left.
Hard cards in the first ball. If the first ball has two hard ones I basically never score.
A red square in my share text. It makes me not want to send anything.
Small text on Mom's phone. The iPad is fine, the phone is squinty.
Words in the meaning line I don't know. If it uses a hard word to explain a hard word, I stop reading it.
If it ever asked me to sign up or put in an email, Mom would say no and that's the end.
must_have_v1: Order the balls easy, then medium, then hard. Ball 1 is all 6 easy cards, so a kid like me can actually score a Goal most days. That's not adding anything, it's just sorting what you already have.
Easy has to mean easy for a 10-year-old who's been playing two years: throw-ins, offside, Messi, Alex Morgan, slang. Not easy for a dad who watches the EPL.
Hook words a kid can read out loud. If the hook is a foreign club name, that card shouldn't be easy.
Big enough text on a phone, and no timer ever.
A share text that shows my black pentagons and the result, with no red square, ready for Mom to paste.
later: Chalkboard picture cards: is this offside, which ref signal, where's the penalty spot. I'd love these more than any word card, and I'd learn from them.
After I'm out, let me flip through the rest of today's cards to see the answers, no score. I always want to know what the Rangers one was.
The basics stuff for new families, but mixed into the easy cards, not a separate thing I have to find.
The anonymous counter so cards that kids keep missing stop being called easy.
A little sound when the pentagon goes black. Not needed, just fun.
dont_build: Accounts, avatars, a profile, a streak calendar with fire emojis. I'd stop if I felt bad for missing Saturday because I had a game.
Leaderboards. I'd be at the bottom under every high school kid.
A timer or a speed bonus. Slow readers lose for no reason.
Lives, jokers, hints, coins. I'd want them, but they make it feel like a phone game that wants Mom's credit card.
A kids mode or separate kids version. I want the SAME cards as Dad, that's the whole point.
The middle tile locked until the outer five. I'd be fine with it, but I don't need it, and it means I can't save the one I know for last. Try it, but don't spend time on it.

roadmap.step: Make sure hook words are readable and the means line uses simple words
roadmap.why: I pick tiles by reading them. If I can't read them, I can't play, and if I can't read the meaning, I don't learn.

roadmap.step: Share text: number, black pentagons per ball, result word, short link, no red
roadmap.why: This is how Dad, Abuela and Priya hear about it. Make a bad-ish day still look good enough to send.

roadmap.step: Phone text size and tap targets check on a small phone and an iPad
roadmap.why: I play on whatever grown-up device is around. Squinty text loses me fast.

roadmap.step: Chalkboard picture cards, starting with offside, ref signals and field markings
roadmap.why: The best learning thing for kids like me, and it helps my actual games. Do it after the daily loop works, not before.

roadmap.step: Stop there and watch

verdict: I'd play it every morning with my dad and make Mom text our Goals to Abuela, but only if the first ball is truly easy for a kid. If it isn't, I'm out by Thursday.

persona: Theo Nakamura, 10, fourth grader in Shoreline WA, second season of U11 rec (coach usually puts me at left back), plays on Mom's iPhone or the family iPad. Knows players from EA FC at my friend Mateo's house, not from watching whole games.
first_week: Monday: Dad shows me after dinner because his friend texted him a Brace. The arcade thing looks cool, like a real game and not a school thing. I see a ball with words on it: "Rabona," "Rangers FC," "Liga MX," "Offside," "Haaland," "Orange slices." I tap Haaland because I know him. Easy, got it, the tile goes black, nice. I tap Orange slices because it's the slang one, and I get it right because "bussin" is obviously right. Then I tap Offside and I THINK I know it but the sentence is long and I read it twice and pick wrong. Red X, shake, and that's it. Done. Zero. Nil. Dad got a Goal. I ask if I can go again and he says no, it's one a day. I'm kind of mad, and I go play something else. Tuesday: I almost don't play. Mom asks me in the car to the dentist, so I play on her phone. This time I only tap stuff I really know and skip the scary words. I get all 5 outside tiles and the middle one unlocks, and it's a hard one about Serie A. I guess. I get it RIGHT by luck and the ball fills up and I get a goal. Then ball two has "Bundesliga" and "Ligue 1" and stuff I can't even say, and I'm out on the second tile. But I got a GOAL. I make Mom text Dad "1 goal." Wednesday: Mateo is over and we play mine together, arguing about every answer. We get one goal again. That was the most fun day. Thursday: I forget. Friday: I go out on the first ball because every tile was pro league stuff. Zero again. I'm like, this is for grown-ups. Saturday after my game: Dad asks if I did Triviela and I say "it's too hard." If the first ball were stuff a kid can actually get, I'd have gotten a goal almost every day and I'd still be playing.
play_daily: Maybe, leaning no. I'd play it when a grown-up reminds me or when Mateo is over. The honest reason I'd stop: if I go out with zero goals on most days, I'll decide it's a dad game. One goal has to be something a 10-year-old who's learning gets most days. Hat trick can be impossible for me, I don't care. But zero almost every day means I quit by week two.
share: I don't have my own phone, so "texting" means making Mom text Dad at work or Grandpa, or sending from the iPad to Mateo. I'd only share on days I got at least one goal, and especially if I beat Dad. That's the whole reason: beating Dad. A Nil I'd never send. The ⚽⚽ part is good because I get it without reading. Rows of black dots and a red square I'd like too, because I could show how close I got. Don't put words in it I have to explain, like "Brace." I learned what that means from the game and that's cool, but Grandpa might not know either. Mostly I'd show it at practice in person, holding up the phone.
love: Picking which tile to answer. I can go for the ones I know first. That's the best part, like I'm choosing my play
The ball turning black and filling up. It feels like scoring
The middle tile being the shot on goal after the five around it. That makes sense to me right away
Short sentences and only three buttons. I can read it
Finding out the answer after, even when I miss. I learned what a rabona is and then I tried one at practice
The slang cards. Those are the ones I win against Dad
Same game for everybody, so I can say to Dad at dinner 'did you get the Arsenal one?'
The arcade look. It doesn't look like homework
turn_offs: Going out with zero on my first or second card because all six tiles were pro league stuff. That's the thing that makes me quit
Tiles I can't even read or say, like Bundesliga, Ligue 1, Serie A, all on one ball. I don't know what to tap
Long sentences. If I have to read it twice I start guessing
Tiny pixel text on the phone. Big is better
No goal sound or anything when I score. It should feel like a GOAL, not just turn black
Being told 'come back tomorrow' right after I lose on card two. I'd want SOMETHING to do, even just look at the answers
Grown-up words in the results that I don't get
must_have_v1: Ball one is the 6 easy cards, ball two medium, ball three hard. That way kids like me can get a goal and grown-ups still have something hard to chase
Easy really means easy for a kid who's learning: famous players, basic rules, ball words, slang. Not 'easy for someone who watches the EPL'
A big goal moment when the ball fills: the net shakes, a sound, something. No words needed
The share text with ⚽ emojis I don't have to read, sent from Mom's phone
Text big enough to read on a phone without squinting, and short sentences on the easy cards
later: Picture cards on the chalkboard pitch: is this offside, which ref signal, name this field line. Those are the ones I could get even if I read slowly, and they'd help me at real games
A basics category for kids and new families, which also fills up the easy pile
The anonymous counter so cards that kids keep missing stop being called easy
After you go out, let me flip through the cards I didn't get to with the answers showing, no score. Just so the day doesn't end in two seconds
Dark mode for playing in the car at night
dont_build: A timer. I read slowly. A timer means I lose to the clock, not because I didn't know it
Leaderboards or accounts. I'm 10, I can't make an account anyway, and seeing I'm last is worse than nothing
Extra lives or jokers. Honestly one miss is fair if the first ball is fair
Endless mode. I'd play it for an hour once and then never do the daily
Badges, streak counters, coins, unlockable stuff. That's the stuff that makes Mom take the iPad away
Lots of tutorials or instructions. I figured it out by tapping. Just keep it obvious

roadmap.step: Have real 10-year-olds play the easy pile and pull out anything most of them miss

persona: Noor Haddad, 13, 8th grade in Shoreline WA, right back on a U14 girls' club team, Reign and Barça Femení fan, phone has Screen Time limits and lives in the team group chat "G14 🍀"
first_week: Monday: my teammate Ava drops a link in the group chat with "⚽ Goal" and nothing else. I open it in the car on the way to practice. The cabinet looks cool, kind of retro-aesthetic, like something you'd see on a TikTok edit. No instructions, I just tap a tile that says "Rabona" because I know that one. Right, it goes black, satisfying. I pick "Portland Thorns" next, then a slang one, then one that says "Rangers FC" which I've never heard of. I guess. Wrong. Day over, 4 cards in. I'm annoyed but the means line taught me something, and the fill-in was quick. I send "Nil 💀" to the chat. Tuesday: I save the Liga MX and Serie A tiles for last on purpose and get a Goal. I send it to the chat and to my dad, who plays too and gets a Nil, which is the best part of my day. Wednesday: I go out on a hard card about the 1990s World Cup. Still fine. I want to see my streak and there isn't one, so I'm less hooked. Thursday: I forget until 10pm. The warm white cabinet is bright in a dark room. I play anyway because three girls on my team posted. Friday: a Kid Slang card uses a word nobody my age says anymore and I screenshot it to roast it. Honestly that screenshot got more replies than my score. Saturday is a game day, I forget. By the end of the week, whether I keep playing depends 90% on whether my team keeps posting, and 10% on whether I keep dying early on men's leagues from countries I don't watch.
play_daily: Maybe, leaning yes if my team plays it. It's short enough for a car ride and the same-cards-for-everyone thing makes it a group chat thing. I'll drop off if it feels like a men's European league quiz where I go out on card 3 most days, or if there's nothing that tracks that I came back (a streak).
share: Yes, every day I do okay, to the team group chat first, then my best friend and my dad (to flex on him). I wouldn't post it on TikTok or Insta. More likely: a grid that shows where I went out (⚫⚫⚫⚫⚫⚫ ⚫⚫🟥) so people can see I was close, a streak number, and one-tap copy. Even more likely: a card so cringe or so hard I have to screenshot it. Less likely: a long share text, a link that looks spammy, anything that spoils answers (my friends would get mad), or a Nil with no way to make it look less embarrassing.
love: Everyone gets the same cards, so we can argue about the hard one at practice
Picking which tile to answer: I can save the Bundesliga one for last and that feels like strategy, not luck
The tile going solid black like a ball patch, and a fresh ball showing up after a goal
The means line: I actually learned the keeper-holds-the-ball rule from it and told my coach
It's short. Under 3 minutes on a good day, about 30 seconds on a bad one
Hat trick for a perfect day. I'd lose my mind if I ever got one
The middle tile as the shot on goal. It makes it feel like soccer and not just a quiz
No ads, no account, no asking for my email
turn_offs: Going out on card 2 to a Serie A or Liga MX fact I could never know. Easy cards need to really be easy for a kid who plays but doesn't watch every league
If the daily mix is mostly men's European soccer. I play. I watch NWSL, the USWNT, Barça Femení. If those barely show up, it's not for me
Kid Slang that adults wrote and that's already dead. A little cringe is funny, but too much and it feels like a parent trying too hard
Not seeing the answer to the one that knocked me out. I need to know
Bright warm white at night when my whole phone is in dark mode
Any 'Great job!' or cartoon cheering, or anything that looks like a school learning app
Words I don't know with no clue at all. 'Brace' was confusing the first time, but I worked it out from the emoji count

A one-tap copy share with a spoiler-free grid that shows where I went out, plus the day number
After a miss: show the right answer and its means line, and on the end screen, the card that got me

A streak counter for days played (saved on the device, nothing fancy). That's what makes me open it on a lazy day
later: Chalkboard picture cards: offside or not, which ref signal, goal or no goal. Those are the ones my team would actually know better than parents

Dark mode
A Basics category for new players. Not for me, but my little sister would play
Yesterday's answers or an archive, so if I miss a game day I can still catch up
dont_build: Leaderboards or accounts. The group chat is the leaderboard
Endless mode, extra lives, hints or jokers. The one-miss rule is why it matters
Push notifications or anything that nags. My Screen Time is already a fight with my mom
Avatars, badges, unlockables or cosmetics

persona: Mateo Okafor-Reyes, 13, eighth grader in Shoreline, center mid on a U14 boys' club team, Arsenal fan because of his uncle, watches highlights on TikTok and YouTube Shorts and is in four group chats, but the team chat is the one that matters
first_week:
Monday: my teammate Jonah drops "Triviela #42 ⚽ Goal" in the team chat with no explanation. That's how I find it. Nobody would ever send me a link with a pitch. I tap it during lunch. The arcade look made me go "ok this is kinda hard." It looks like a retro FIFA menu, not a school website. First ball is easy. I tap "Rabona" first because I know that one, then the Arsenal one. I get the middle tile and score a goal. Second ball I go out on a Liga MX card about some club in Monterrey. I've never watched Liga MX in my life. One goal. I'm mad, but it's my fault for tapping that tile, so I'm not mad at the game. I send "⚽ Goal, the Liga MX one is rigged" to the chat.

Tuesday: I play before practice because Jonah got a brace and I'm not letting that stand. I go out on ball 1, card 4, an offside rule thing I should've known. Nil. That stings more than anything because I PLAY. I don't send it. Then I send it anyway an hour later because Ethan sent a Nil too.

Wednesday and Thursday: it's routine now. I play on the bus. It takes me like 90 seconds. I figured out the strategy is to tap the tiles you know first and leave the scary one for last, and that feels smart. Thursday I learn the keeper six-second thing changed. I bring it up at practice and our coach didn't know. That's the best thing that happened all week honestly.

Friday: someone in the chat gets a hat trick and posts it in caps. Everyone is pressed. That's peak. Saturday is a game day and I forget until 9pm and play in bed. Sunday I'm kind of tired of seeing Bundesliga and Serie A cards I can only guess on. If the hard ball is all "which year did this Italian club win" I'll stop trying past ball 2. If there are hard cards that are hard because they're about rules or players I actually know, I'll keep grinding.
play_daily: Yes, but only because of the group chat. The game alone, maybe 3 days a week. The game plus seeing Jonah's result every morning means every day, because I can't let him have it. If it takes more than 2 minutes or needs a login, no.
share: Yes, to the team group chat, every day I get at least a Goal. A Nil I'll only send if someone else already sent one. Brothers and my uncle get the Arsenal-related ones screenshotted. More likely to share: the rows showing exactly where I went out (⚽⚽🟥) so people can see I almost had a hat trick, a share that's ONE tap to copy and doesn't spoil the answer, and a puzzle number so we know we played the same one. Less likely: anything with a long link, a "Can you beat me?" type message pre-written for me (cringe, I'd delete it), or a share image I have to save. Text only. It has to look normal in iMessage.
love: Same 18 cards for everyone. That's the whole reason it works in a group chat
Picking which tile to answer. It makes going out feel like my fault, not luck, and that's why I come back instead of quitting
One miss and you're done. It's brutal, but it makes a hat trick actually mean something
The answer and the 'means' line after I miss. I actually learned rule stuff I bring up at practice
The arcade cabinet look. It doesn't look like homework or a kids' app
Goal, Brace, Hat trick as the result names. Those are words I already use

Going out on card 1 or 2 too often. If the easy ball isn't actually easy, I'd stop after a few Nils
Anything that asks for my email, name or a login. Instant close
A share message that sounds like an adult wrote it
must_have_v1: Same daily 18 cards for everyone, with a puzzle number and a clear reset time

persona: Jen Halvorsen, 44, Shoreline WA, physical therapy assistant. Her daughter Maya (13) plays center back on a U14 club team and her son Theo (9) plays rec. She learned the game from the sideline about six years ago, and she's one of 19 parents in the team group text.

But I'm annoyed, because Jess got a Goal and I got Nil on my first day ever. If I'd known I could skip around more carefully I'd have saved the scary-word tile for last. Lesson learned.

Day 2: Now I play strategically. I tap every hook I recognize first: Arsenal, Rapinoe, World Cup 2026. Leave "Rangers FC" and "Pressing" for last. I get 5 on the first ball, then the middle tile is a Laws of the Game card about the keeper holding the ball too long. I guessed penalty, it was a corner kick. Out at 5 of 6. So close it physically hurt, which is exactly why I'll be back tomorrow. I text Jess the 🟥 row because 5 black dots and a red card is funny.

Day 3: First Goal. I screenshot it before I even remember there's a share button. Second ball is medium and I go out on a Serie A nickname. Fine. Banked a goal, I feel smart.

Day 5: Goal. One of the cards was about offside and I read the means line twice. Learned more about offside from one blank than from three men explaining it at a bar.
